highlights.summary: Paramount is appointing a new co-CEO ahead of the close of its $110 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery. Ynon Kreiz, previously Mattel's chairman and CEO, will be joining Paramount to lead alongside chairman and CEO David Ellison.
body: Mattel chairman and CEO Ynon Kreiz is joining Paramount to help David Ellison run the company.

According to Paramount, “Ellison will focus on the company’s long-term strategy, creative vision and direction, including its talent relationships, strategic partnerships, technology and capital allocation. Kreiz will focus on the company’s day-to-day management and integration of the combined businesses.” The combined Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery will “report jointly” to Ellison and Kreiz.
Kreiz joined Mattel in 2018. While he was leading the company, it launched the hit Barbie film in partnership with Warner Bros. Pictures. His first day at Paramount is October 5th.
Today, a judge also approved Paramount’s recently-announced settlement in a lawsuit with several states that had been blocking the Warner Bros. Discovery merger, according to Reuters.

highlights.title: Price books Clayton showdown at World Grand Prix as Aspinall races through
highlights.summary: Gerwyn Price set up an all-Welsh quarter-final showdown with Jonny Clayton with a straight-sets win over Ross Smith at the World Grand Prix, as Ryan Joyce and Nathan Aspinall also progressed in Leicester.
body: Price, among the tournament favourites after Luke Littler's shock early exit, followed his opening-round victory over Sebastian Białecki by dropping just four legs to despatch Smith at the Mattioli Arena.

The 2020 champion was outscored by Smith - having posted the highest average of the first round - but dropped just four legs during his 3-0 win, securing him a meeting with World Cup of Darts partner Clayton on Friday evening.

Clayton opened with three consecutive ton-plus checkouts and made four in total during a 3-1 victory over Wessel Nijman, where a 93.08 average and some remarkable finishing pushed him past the 12th seed.

Ryan Joyce breezed into the quarter-finals with a straight-sets victory over Danny Noppert, as Luke Woodhouse - who stunned Littler in the first round - was knocked out after losing 3-0 to Nathan Aspinall in a one-sided contest.

highlights.title: Google announces Gemini 4 and says it’s so capable that only ‘trusted cyber defenders’ can have it right now
highlights.summary: Google today revealed its next AI frontier model, which it's calling Gemini 4 Argon. The new model delivers "frontier performance in complex workflows across real-world software engineering, enterprise knowledge work like legal and finance, and cybersecurity defense," according to chief AI…
body: Gemini 4 Argon is launching first in a limited capacity so Google can make sure it’s not misaligned.

Kavukcuoglu says Gemini 4 Argon is already powering Google’s “internal workflows,” highlighting how the model has helped with tasks like large-scale codebase migrations. Google also shared a big chart showing many benchmarks where Gemini 4 fares better than competing models from OpenAI and Anthropic. (The AI community was buzzing earlier this week on X over what appeared to be leaked benchmarks for the new model.) Google will be strengthening “critical frontier safeguards” before a broader rollout, including defending against misuse and prompt injection attacks and monitoring for misalignment.

The launch of Gemini 4 Argon comes just a day after OpenAI’s splashy DevDay conference, where OpenAI launched its Dots AI agent and GPT-6.1 Sol AI model. (OpenAI also said this week that it wouldn’t be releasing a planned GPT-6.1 Astra model due to worries about safety.) It’s also arriving soon after Kavukcuoglu’s appointment as the new boss of DeepMind in August.

highlights.title: Europe's CPC targets King, Supercell, Mojang and others over virtual currencies
highlights.summary: Europe's Consumer Protection Cooperation Network is taking "coordinated actions" against a string of top games companies as it looks to investigate compliance with 'Key Principles' on in-game virtual currencies announced last year.
body: The CPC is a network of national authorities responsible for the enforcement of EU consumer protection laws. It has asked Activision Blizzard, Crytek, InnoGames, King, Mojang, Plarium, PLR Worldwide Sales, Riot Games, Supercell and Ubisoft to bring their commercial practices in line relating to in-game virtual currencies.

Games being assessed include Hunt: Showdown 1896, Forge of Empires, Candy Crush Saga, Minecraft, Mech Arena, Gardenscapes, Valorant, Clash of Clans, For Honor, Diablo Immortal and Call of Duty Mobile.

The games were selected for assessment by the CPC Network "in the context of a wide-scale market compliance check due to broad reach, cross-device accessibility, and varied age ratings, all of which amplify the impact of the practices on consumers".
It's not clear what, if any, 'Key Principles' have not been adhered to prior to the CPC Network opening its investigations.

highlights.title: The Battle to Be Your Personal AI Agent Is Here
highlights.summary: OpenAI's Dots and Meta's Muse are vying to be your AI agent of choice. I've tried both—and I suspect you will too.
body: Yesterday, I spent the morning at OpenAI ’s annual DevDay, where over 2,500 nerds discussed building software and marveled at the latest artificial intelligence models. The biggest reveal of the day was Dots, the company’s new, always-on agents that proactively help complete tasks and make autonomous decisions as they scour the web.

After watching the sometimes messy demos on stage and hearing CEO Sam Altman talk about his experiences using the agents, I was curious what it felt like to boss my own Dot around. I’ve spent most of September testing another cute, cuddly agent, Meta’s Muse, and I wanted to know how OpenAI’s user experience would compare.

I named mine “Toolie” and tweaked it to look like a pink frog. As midnight approached and my partner slept soundly nearby, I started whispering sweet nothings to Toolie. I called my personalized bot through ChatGPT, asking what tasks it was best at. “My strongest work is taking a messy, time-consuming task and turning it into something you can use,” it responded. OK, sure. Let’s get to work.
points: OpenAI's Dots and Meta's Muse are vying to be your AI agent of choice.

body: Overton saw him collect a PCA awards quadruple, winning the PCA Men's Player of the Year trophy, the PCA Men's Domestic Overall MVP, the Rothesay County Championship Player of the Year and selection in the IG PCA Men's Team of the Year.

The 32-year-old, who has scored 951 runs, taken 76 wickets and 45 catches across all three formats this season, becomes the first Somerset player to secure the award since Nick Compton in 2012, beating competition from the notable shortlist of players including Joe Clarke, George Hill and Dan Lawrence.
He also scored a memorable unbeaten 79 in the Vitality Blast quarter-finals to take Somerset to Finals Day.
"It's a phenomenal feeling. To be chosen by your peers to win this award is very special; it means so much to me," said Overton.

highlights.title: Ace Combat 8’s Stellar Multiplayer Reveals the Terrors of Live-Service Games
highlights.summary: Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is one of the best games I’ve played this year. Its 25-hour single-player campaign, featuring 30 thrilling missions, is worth the price of admission alone.
body: Due to the nature of online servers, I wasn’t able to play much Ace Combat Online ahead of Ace Combat 8 ’s review embargo. I only had access to the mode for a few hours, where I moved through a blitz of rotating playlists with press and creators, rather than the wider player population who’s playing now — not substantial enough to pass much judgment. Now that Ace Combat Online is live (at least for the diehards who preordered the base game), I have a much better feel for its multiplayer, and it comes with some real highs and lows. The moment-to-moment action is tense and exciting, but you’ll need to wade through a lot of menus and live-service headaches to appreciate it.

When you first pop into Ace Combat Online, the experience can be immediately overwhelming. After creating a character, you’re dropped into a Destiny-like social hub lined with other players and vendors. Loading into a mission, checking challenges, editing planes, buying new gear, managing your squad — everything is split between various NPCs. It takes a bit of time to figure out where every feature you need lives.
points: Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is one of the best games I’ve played this year.

highlights.title: Dinosaur-killing impact crater might have been teeming with life
highlights.summary: About 66 million years ago, the Chicxulub asteroid smashed into Earth, kicking up tsunamis and dropping hot debris that annihilated non-avian dinosaurs and many other species. But not everything it left in its wake was destructive.
body: When researchers drilled for samples in the impact zone in 2016, they studied the types of rock that had formed as a result of the asteroid strike. This gave more insight into what happened in the immediate and long-term aftermath of this cataclysmic event.

The collision was intense enough to cause deformation far beneath the surface. Subterranean effects reached 35 km (almost 22 miles) down, and included the melting an immense amount of rock. Exposure to seawater made that rock porous. As hot water seeped into the pores, a hydrothermal system formed. The hot water gushing into an isolated region of the freezing depths could have attracted microorganisms and possibly other life forms that were otherwise struggling to survive.

highlights.title: There Are Plenty of Reasons to Be Concerned About Bioweapons Development—Even Without AI
highlights.summary: In her new book on biological warfare, Annie Jacobsen didn’t even discuss AI because scientists can already warp Mother Nature to create extinction-level events.
body: This story originally appeared on Mother Jones and is part of the Climate Desk collaboration.

We’ve been hearing a great deal recently about the specter of AI-driven human extinction. Maybe our misplaced trust in AI intelligence will set off World War III. Or AI agents will unleash widespread cyberattacks and take over the internet. Given too much autonomy, the machines will run amok. They may seek to deceive their creators—wait, that’s already happened. Suppose they conclude, like Agent Smith in The Matrix, that “human beings … are a plague, and we are the cure.” Or perhaps the chatbots help bad humans unleash a literal plague—a biological weapon.

That last one isn’t merely theoretical. A “misuse” report Anthropic made public earlier this month detailed five cases in which foreign scientists tried to evade Claude’s guardrails on “gain of function” inquiries. That’s a euphemism for when scientists tinker with a pathogen’s genes to enhance it in some way, making it more infectious, deadlier, or better able to spread among mammals, for example.
points: In her new book on biological warfare, Annie Jacobsen didn’t even discuss AI because scientists can already warp Mother Nature to create extinction-level events.

highlights.title: Gill hits 223 not out as India chase down 406 to beat West Indies in second ODI
highlights.summary: A capacity crowd witnessed a host of batting records on Wednesday, Shubman Gill leading the way with 223 not out off 133 balls as India beat West Indies by eight wickets in their second ODI.
body: Gill notched his best ODI score and a record-high individual tally in an ODI run-chase. It was his 11th hundred in the format, one of five on the day, as India amassed 406-2 in 43.3 overs to take a winning 2-0 lead in the three-match series.
Opening partner Rohit Sharma made 101 as the duo put on 255 off 158 balls - the second-highest opening stand for India in ODIs.
It was the second successful 400-plus run-chase in ODI history, after South Africa's record 438-9 against Australia in 2006.

Earlier, three West Indies batters struck centuries in an ODI innings for the first time. Amir Jangoo top-scored with 114, skipper Shai Hope made 104 and opener John Campbell set the day's tempo with 101 off 68 balls.

highlights.title: Fifth unvaccinated person dies of measles; CDC still not counting all deaths
highlights.summary: A fifth, unvaccinated person has died of measles in Pennsylvania, the state's health department announced Wednesday. The department identified the deceased as a resident of Lancaster County, which is the epicenter of a raging outbreak that began in late April.
body: Lancaster County has reported 381 cases and three of the five deaths in the outbreak. The previous two deaths were both in infants too young to be vaccinated. That includes a newborn boy and a 6-week-old baby girl. So far, no other information has been released about the county’s third death announced today.

The other two deaths were in an unvaccinated 18-year-old resident of Mifflin County, who developed a severe neurological complication of measles, and an unvaccinated 40-year-old woman, who had several chronic underlying health conditions that put her at higher risk of severe infection, including chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).

Prior to these five deaths in Pennsylvania, the state had not reported a measles death in 35 years. To date, they are the only measles deaths reported this year in the US. Last year, the US saw three measles deaths: two in otherwise-healthy, unvaccinated school-aged children in Texas and an unvaccinated adult in New Mexico. All three were connected to a massive measles outbreak in West Texas, which spilled over to nearby states. Prior to the 2025 deaths, the US had not seen a measles death since 2015.

highlights.title: The AI Tamagotchis are coming
highlights.summary: While AI has made plenty of inroads on people's phones and computers, it's largely failed in dedicated devices. But over the next year, two major AI companies, Meta and OpenAI, will attempt to change that.
body: Personal AI hardware has mostly crashed and burned. OpenAI and Meta are counting on two selling points: It’s useful, and it’s cute.

“Hardware is hard” is a tech industry mantra. Dedicated AI devices like the Friend and Humane AI Pin have inspired mainly frustration and backlash, which may only worsen as public anger toward AI grows. Meta and OpenAI, however, are both pushing ahead. OpenAI is working with famed ex-Apple designer Jony Ive and plans to ship no earlier than February 2027, per a public filing. Meta aims to launch a pendant-like device sooner, before this year’s holiday shopping season.

While OpenAI’s hardware didn’t make an appearance at this year’s DevDay, the company debuted a major new AI agent platform called Dots, complete with personalizable colored blobs with eyes. During a Q&A with reporters after the keynote, when asked whether Dots would make their way into a future physical hardware device, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman replied that that “seems like a very reasonable thing to assume we may do someday,” declining to offer further details.
points: While AI has made plenty of inroads on people's phones and computers, it's largely failed in dedicated devices.
But over the next year, two major AI companies, Meta and OpenAI, will attempt to change that.

body: Speaking on the Deconstructor of Fun podcast, Pincus shared that he had a handshake agreement with Supercell CEO Ilkka Paananen to acquire the Finnish developer for $400 million in cash.
“I went to my board, and they were grumpy and they said, until you prove you can manage what you have, we don’t want you to buy anything else.”

highlights.title: Stella McCartney makes waves with ‘sea life, not sea food’ theme in zero-wool Paris show
highlights.summary: Designer showcases wool alternatives and ocean-inspired clothes and says ‘kindness requires real work’ Stella McCartney has been talking about animal rights at fashion week for 30 years. She is usually a lone voice, but the issue is back in the headlines this season.
body: “There is no wool on the runway this season, and I’m proud of that,” McCartney said after her show. She has been working on wool alternatives, including Brewed Protein, a fermented alternative to cashmere and wool developed in collaboration with the Japanese biotech firm Spiber, which was first used in her collections a year ago.

The issue, she says, is “a tricky one. I’ve got alpacas at home, and I have to shear them. If you can shear a sheep in a kind, humane way, then I don’t, personally, think that’s the end of the world. When we do have wool in our collections it is responsibly sourced. But the way a lot of [wool production] is done today is deeply cruel.

“At the end of the day it’s about how kind you are, but monitoring that kindness requires real work. At Stella, we police everything from start to finish at my cost, at my time. If I use wool, I can show you exactly where it’s coming from, and I’m proud of that. But I’m alone in that, and I shouldn’t be.”

highlights.title: Returning from vacation? The government can search your phone without a warrant.
highlights.summary: An Argentinian-American writer and immigration advocate recently sued the federal government, demanding that it delete data that he believes was copied off of his phone when he re-entered the United States earlier this month.
body: According to the seven-page complaint, Thomas Kennedy said that a Customs and Border Protection agent at Miami International Airport physically searched his bags, questioned him about his books and magazines, and then demanded that he hand over his phone.

“[The agent] threatened me, saying that if I didn’t give him my phone, my interrogation was going to take much longer and they could retain my phone indefinitely,” Kennedy wrote. “I felt like I had no choice, so I handed my phone to the CBP agent.”
The agent took the phone away and only returned after approximately 45 minutes, during which Kennedy believes that data on the phone was copied. He was then released with no charges.
The activist says there is a significant amount of sensitive personal and professional information on his phone, and he is now seeking that the government delete this data.

highlights.summary: If you're a big fan of racing games, you've probably already got yourself a wheel. But if you're still rocking an entry level gear- or belt-driven wheel because you've been held back by the steep cost of direct drive, then check out this new deal.
body: The R5 is not Moza's least expensive direct drive wheel. That honor goes to the Moza R3, which retails for $279.99 and is not currently on sale. The primary difference between the two is maximum torque: the R5 offers 5.5Nm of force compared to 3.9Nm from the R3. Both are less expensive than other alternatives: Logitech's G RS50 is $600 (for the wheel only), Fanatec's CSL DD Ready2Race Bundle is $540, Simagic's Green Flag Bundle is $600, and Thrustmaster's T598 is $466. Some do offer advantages like a higher torque ceiling or console compatibility, but if value is king it's hard to beat Moza.

So what makes direct drive the gold standard for racing sims? Direct drive wheels connect directly to the motor, which translates to immediate force feedback with zero latency and no lost power delivery from gear or belt-drive resistance. The higher the torque rating, the wider range of sensitivity. The Moza R5 is a big step up in immersion compared to a gear or belt driven wheel, and 5Nm is considered the baseline for bringing out the best of what direct drive has to offer.

highlights.title: All the latest news on Meta’s cute, creepy Muse AI agent
highlights.summary: Meta launched a new Muse AI agent it claims can help you with everything from firing off emails to buying stuff online. Muse can be surprisingly effective at delivering on those promises — if you’re willing to trust Meta with your data and hand Muse your credit card.
body: Tech YouTuber Matt Robb says that Muse gave out his home address to a total stranger this weekend, after authorizing the bot to handle his Facebook Marketplace account. That’s despite Meta placing great emphasis on the security features of Muse when it launched the personal AI agent earlier this month as it tries to catch up with competing AI providers like Anthropic and OpenAI.

“Just found out it told people my address and agreed a lowball price and then they showed up without it even telling me until late tonight that it messed up,” Robb said on Threads, providing a screenshot of Muse’s admission. “[Muse] didn’t tell me any of this until after the guy had left (luckily I’m in an apartment with security),” he added in a follow up post.

Meta says in a blog post today that Muse can now connect to more productivity apps, which it’s pitching as a way to make the agent more helpful for small businesses. Muse has already been able to connect to apps like Gmail and Outlook, but now the list includes Asana, Box, Canva, Dropbox, Figma, Notion, Slack, Stripe, Zoom, and more. Meta also says that Muse will be able to access Facebook and Instagram business accounts.

OL Lyonnes had scored eight times in their first fixture in the league phase, away against the Swiss side Servette, but Chelsea looked comfortable for large periods and Bompastor said: “I’m really proud of my team, being able to not concede here. We are happy also with the ball, the way we performed, we were able to exploit different spaces. The only thing that was missing was the goal.”

The French side had scored at least seven times in all four matches they had played in all competitions this season. Given that formidable form and the confidence in the hosts’ front line, Chelsea were grateful to Hannah Hampton for her sharp save from Salma Paralluelo on 20 minutes, and similarly glad to see Melchie Dumornay’s powerful effort fizz just wide of a post a few minutes later.

highlights.title: Colman Domingo on the Elegance of All-Black Luggage
highlights.summary: The star of Euphoria, Sing Sing, and The Four Seasons' travel hacks include J.Crew-taught folding skills, packing cubes full of fragrances, and plenty of gummy bears.
body: Colman Domingo is always on the move. The Emmy-winning actor kicked off our call by warning me that the famed bells of Reykjavik may ring in the background during our chat—having arrived in Iceland after a quick turnaround from Santa Fe, jet-setting from one location to another to film the third season of his Netflix hit The Four Seasons, along with co-stars Tina Fey, Will Forte, Kerri Kenney-Silver, Marco Calvani, and Erika Henningsen.

“I move pretty quickly,” the 56-year-old Philadelphia native told Condé Nast Traveler. As a result, there's one aspect of travel he's totally mastered: “I'm very proud of my packing style—I’ve got it down to a science.”

Case in point: He only had a few hours at home between those trips, having arrived back in Malibu from New Mexico at 10:30 p.m. before a morning flight to Iceland. But that was plenty of time for the pro. “We got in, did laundry, packed, and were in bed by 11:45 p.m.,” he said.

It all stems from the precision he learned during his early jobs at J. Crew and Banana Republic. “Everything is very organized and well-folded—I love packing like I’m still working there,” he said. “I’m pretty detailed about my packing.”
